title: Account Management
statement: Define allowed/prohibited account types; create/enable/modify/disable/remove accounts per policy.
Specify authorized users, group/role membership, and privileges; authorize based on valid authorization and intended usage; monitor use.
Disable expired, inactive (ODP), orphaned, policy-violating, or high-risk accounts.
Notify account managers within ODP periods on departure/transfer/need-to-know change.
Require logout after ODP inactivity (behavior); automatic lock is 03.01.10.

odps.text: Users log out after [time period] of expected inactivity

linux.summary: Account types, lifecycle, inactivity lock, and TMOUT via useradd/usermod, shadow, systemd-logind, and login.defs.

title: Access Enforcement
statement: Enforce approved authorizations for logical access to CUI and system resources per access-control policy.

linux.summary: Enforce DAC/MAC: umask 027, home 0750, shadow 0000, sudoers, optional SELinux targeted enforcing.

title: Information Flow Enforcement
statement: Enforce approved authorizations controlling the flow of CUI within the system and between connected systems.

linux.summary: nftables/firewalld zones, rp_filter, and no forwarding of CUI in the clear.

title: Separation of Duties
statement: Identify duties requiring separation; define system access authorizations to support that separation.

linux.summary: Partial: wheel vs audit group split; sudoers so audit admins are not general sysadmins.

title: Least Privilege
statement: Allow only access necessary for assigned tasks.
Authorize access to ODP security functions and security-relevant information.
Review privileges at ODP frequency; reassign or remove as needed.

odps.defaultValue: account mgmt, sudoers, auditd, firewall, crypto keys, package install

linux.summary: Least privilege via sudo -l, no NOPASSWD, no uid 0 aliases, periodic review of wheel.

title: Least Privilege – Privileged Accounts
statement: Restrict privileged accounts to ODP personnel/roles.
Require non-privileged accounts for non-security functions.

linux.summary: PermitRootLogin no; root shell only on console; admins use unprivileged accounts + sudo.

title: Least Privilege – Privileged Functions
statement: Prevent non-privileged users from executing privileged functions; log execution of privileged functions.

linux.summary: Prevent non-privileged execution of privileged functions; log sudo and usermod via auditd.

title: Unsuccessful Logon Attempts
statement: Limit consecutive invalid logons during an ODP window.
Automatically lock/delay/notify when the limit is exceeded.

odps.text: Lock duration or until admin release

linux.summary: pam_faillock: deny 3, fail_interval 900, unlock_time 900.

title: System Use Notification
statement: Display a system-use notification with privacy and security notices consistent with CUI rules before granting access.

odps.defaultValue: This system processes CUI. Unauthorized use is prohibited. Use may be monitored.

linux.summary: CUI banner in /etc/issue and /etc/issue.net; Banner in sshd.

title: Device Lock
statement: Initiate a device lock after ODP inactivity and/or require user-initiated lock.
Retain the lock until re-authentication; conceal previously visible information.

linux.summary: logind IdleAction=lock after idle; GDM screensaver; ssh ClientAlive as defense in depth.

title: Session Termination
statement: Terminate a user session automatically after ODP conditions or trigger events.

odps.defaultValue: 900s idle; end of shift; incident lockout

linux.summary: TMOUT plus sshd ClientAliveInterval/CountMax terminate idle sessions.

title: Remote Access
statement: Establish usage, configuration, and connection requirements for each allowable remote access type; authorize before connecting.
Route remote access through managed access-control points; authorize remote privileged commands.

linux.summary: SSH only via managed bastion; AllowUsers/AllowGroups; no gateway ports; Match for privileged remote.

args.block:
AllowGroups wheel
GatewayPorts no
PermitRootLogin no
MaxAuthTries {{ odp.max_auth_tries }}

title: Wireless Access
statement: Establish usage/configuration/connection requirements; authorize each wireless type; disable unused radios before issuance; authenticate and encrypt wireless access.

linux.summary: Disable Wi-Fi/Bluetooth when unused; NetworkManager wifi.backend none; rfkill.

title: Access Control for Mobile Devices
statement: Establish usage/configuration/connection requirements; authorize connections; full-device or container encryption for CUI on mobile devices.

linux.summary: Partial: usbguard or usb_storage blacklist; LUKS for laptop storage. MDM policy is organizational.

remediate.title: usbguard
remediate.notes: Requires a device policy; do not enable blindly on desktops that need HID.

title: Use of External Systems
statement: Prohibit unauthorized external systems; require ODP security requirements; verify SSP satisfaction and retain connection agreements; restrict org-controlled portable media on external systems.

odps.defaultValue: Same 800-171r3 overlay; no CUI on unmanaged endpoints

linux.summary: Partial: no default routes to unmanaged nets; ssh Match deny from unknown; documented ISA.

title: Publicly Accessible Content
statement: Train authorized individuals so public content does not contain CUI; review and remove CUI if discovered.

linux.summary: Partial: find CUI markings on web roots; no httpd serving /CUI.

title: Literacy Training and Awareness
statement: Provide security literacy training at hire, at ODP frequency, on change/events, covering insider threat, social engineering, and social mining; update content on ODP cadence.

title: Role-Based Training
statement: Provide role-based security training before access/duties and at ODP frequency; update content on ODP cadence.

title: Event Logging
statement: Specify ODP event types selected for logging; review and update at ODP frequency.

odps.defaultValue: logon/logoff, privileged exec, account change, config change, auditd, module load, time change, network

linux.summary: auditd rules covering logon, privilege, account, module, time, and identity events.

title: Audit Record Content
statement: Include type, when, where, source, outcome, and identities; provide additional information as needed.

linux.summary: auditd log_format ENRICHED; audisp for extra identity fields.

title: Audit Record Generation
statement: Generate records for selected events/content; retain for the records-retention policy.

odps.rationale: CMMC/DFARS typical floor; longer if the records schedule requires.

linux.summary: Generate and retain audit records (max_log_file, num_logs) for the ODP retention window.

title: Response to Audit Logging Process Failures
statement: Alert ODP roles within ODP time; take ODP additional actions (overwrite oldest / suspend / halt).

odps.defaultValue: SUSPEND writing when admin space exhausted

linux.summary: space_left_action EMAIL/SYSLOG; admin_space_left_action SUSPEND; disk_full_action SUSPEND.

title: Audit Record Review, Analysis, and Reporting
statement: Review/analyze at ODP frequency; report findings; correlate across repositories.

linux.summary: Partial: aureport + journal + optional rsyslog forwarding to a SIEM. Human review is organizational.

title: Audit Record Reduction and Report Generation
statement: Implement reduction/reporting that preserves original content and time order.

linux.summary: aureport/ausearch remain available; do not overwrite original logs.

title: Time Stamps
statement: Use internal clocks; record stamps at ODP granularity using UTC or a fixed offset.

linux.summary: chronyd with authenticated NTP; UTC; maxslewtime.

title: Protection of Audit Information
statement: Protect audit information and tools from unauthorized access/modification/deletion; restrict audit-management to a subset of privileged users.

linux.summary: audit.log 0600 root:root; audit group for ausearch; immutable rules (-e 2) after load.

title: Baseline Configuration
statement: Develop and maintain a current baseline under configuration control; review/update at ODP frequency and on component change.

linux.summary: Partial: oscap/AIDE baseline snapshot plus documented CMDB. Full CM process is organizational.

title: Configuration Settings
statement: Establish/document/implement ODP configuration settings in the most restrictive mode consistent with operations; document approved deviations.

odps.defaultValue: DISA RHEL 9 STIG + CIS L2 + this overlay

linux.summary: Apply DISA STIG / CIS L2 via oscap remediation plus sysctl, crypto-policies, sshd.

title: Configuration Change Control
statement: Define configuration-controlled change types; review/approve with security-impact consideration; implement, document, monitor.

linux.summary: Partial: etckeeper or git of /etc plus yum history; CAB workflow is organizational.

title: Impact Analyses
statement: Analyze security impacts before implementing changes; verify requirements still hold after change.

title: Access Restrictions for Change
statement: Define, document, approve, and enforce physical and logical access restrictions associated with system changes.

linux.summary: Restrict who can change config: wheel-only visudo, immutable audit rules, no world-writable /etc.

title: Least Functionality
statement: Provide only mission-essential capabilities; prohibit ODP functions/ports/protocols/services; review at ODP frequency; disable/remove unnecessary ones.

odps.defaultValue: telnet, rsh, rlogin, ypserv, tftp, talk, ftp, bluetooth (servers), rpcbind if unused

linux.summary: Mask unused services, remove telnet/rsh/ypserv/tftp, close unused ports.

audit.title: unwanted packages gone
audit.command: rpm -q telnet rsh ypserv tftp talk 2>/dev/null || true

title: Authorized Software – Allow by Exception
statement: Identify authorized programs; deny-all allow-by-exception; review the list at ODP frequency.

linux.summary: fapolicyd deny-all allow-by-exception, or rpm-ostree immutable + dnf versionlock.

remediate.title: enable fapolicyd
remediate.notes: Tune allowlists before enforcing on production.

title: System Component Inventory
statement: Develop/document inventory; review at ODP frequency; update on install/remove/update.

linux.summary: rpm -qa + dnf repoquery + lshw/dmidecode inventory written to /var/lib/nist/inventory.json.

title: Information Location
statement: Identify/document CUI location and the components that process/store it; document location changes.

linux.summary: Partial: label CUI mountpoints (e.g. /srv/cui) and document in inventory.

title: System and Component Configuration for High-Risk Areas
statement: Issue ODP configurations to individuals traveling to high-risk locations; apply ODP requirements on return.

odps.defaultValue: sanitized disk, no CUI, usbguard, VPN-only, reimage on return

linux.summary: Partial: travel image with no CUI, usbguard, and reimage script on return.

title: User Identification and Authentication
statement: Uniquely identify and authenticate users and associate that identity with processes; re-authenticate on ODP circumstances.

linux.summary: Unique UIDs; no shared logins; UsePAM yes; rekey sshd.

title: Device Identification and Authentication
statement: Uniquely identify and authenticate ODP devices before establishing a connection.

odps.defaultValue: hosts in the CUI enclave; admin jump hosts; VPN endpoints

linux.summary: 802.1X or ssh host-based + known_hosts; optionally FreeIPA host principals.

title: Multi-Factor Authentication
statement: Implement MFA for privileged and non-privileged accounts.

linux.summary: MFA via pam_sss + IPA/IdP, or pam_u2f / pam_oath. Do not use google-authenticator as the CUI default (not FIPS).

remediate.title: authselect sssd with-faillock
remediate.notes: Wire a FIPS authenticator (PIV, IPA OTP, FIDO2), not google-authenticator.

title: Replay-Resistant Authentication
statement: Implement replay-resistant authentication for privileged and non-privileged accounts.

linux.summary: SSH protocol 2, PubkeyAuthentication, Kerberos or OTP with nonce; no password-only over the network.

title: Identifier Management
statement: Authorize assignment of identifiers; select/assign; prevent reuse for ODP period; identify individual status characteristic.

linux.summary: Partial: UID reuse prevented via /etc/login.defs UID_MIN and a reserved-UID ledger.

title: Password Management
statement: Maintain and update a compromised-password list; reject listed passwords; transmit only over protected channels; store cryptographically protected; force new password after recovery; enforce ODP composition rules.

odps.defaultValue: minlen 14, dictcheck, minclass 4; no periodic expiry solely for expiry

linux.summary: pwquality minlen 14, dictcheck, pwhistory; SHA512 or yescrypt; no plaintext in transit (sshd only).

title: Authentication Feedback
statement: Obscure feedback of authentication information during authentication.

linux.summary: PAM does not echo passwords; sshd does not log passwords; login.defs PASS_MAX_DAYS optional.

title: Authenticator Management
statement: Verify recipient identity; establish initial content; procedures for issue/loss/revoke; change defaults at first use; refresh on ODP frequency/events; protect authenticator content.

odps.defaultValue: on compromise, role change, or 1 year for hardware tokens; passwords on recovery not calendar

linux.summary: Partial: chage force change on first login; no default vendor passwords; sshd PermitEmptyPasswords no.

title: Incident Handling
statement: Implement incident handling consistent with the IR plan: preparation, detection/analysis, containment, eradication, recovery.

linux.summary: Partial: auditd + fail2ban + systemd coredumpctl feed detection; IR playbook is organizational.

title: Incident Monitoring, Reporting, and Response Assistance
statement: Track/document incidents; report suspected incidents within ODP time to the IR capability and ODP authorities; provide a support resource.

odps.defaultValue: 1 hour for confirmed CUI incident; 24 hours suspected
CISO; contracting officer; CISA as required

linux.summary: Partial: rsyslog/journal forwarding and a local /var/log/incidents dropbox.

title: Incident Response Testing
statement: Test IR capability effectiveness at ODP frequency.

title: Incident Response Training
statement: Train users consistent with roles within ODP time of assuming the role, on change, and at ODP frequency; update content.

title: Incident Response Plan
statement: Develop, distribute, update, and protect an IR plan covering structure, reportable incidents, sharing, and responsibilities.

title: Maintenance Tools
statement: Approve/control/monitor maintenance tools; check diagnostic media for malware; prevent removal of equipment containing CUI.

linux.summary: Partial: rpm -V on diagnostic tools; clamav scan of USB diagnostics before use.

title: Nonlocal Maintenance
statement: Approve and monitor nonlocal maintenance; MFA and replay resistance; terminate session and network connections when complete.

linux.summary: Nonlocal maintenance only over MFA SSH; ForceCommand + Match group maint; idle timeout.

args.block:
Match Group maint
  ForceCommand /usr/sbin/nologin
  AllowTcpForwarding no

title: Maintenance Personnel
statement: Authorize maintainers; keep the list; verify non-escorted personnel have required authorizations; designate escorts otherwise.

linux.summary: Partial: /etc/nist/maint-personnel.list plus sudo -U listing.

title: Media Storage
statement: Physically control and securely store system media that contain CUI.

linux.summary: Partial: LUKS on data disks; sticky-bit on /media; no automount of USB.

title: Media Access
statement: Restrict access to CUI on system media to authorized personnel or roles.

linux.summary: Partial: DAC on CUI mounts plus fscrypt/LUKS.

title: Media Sanitization
statement: Sanitize media containing CUI prior to disposal, release out of control, or reuse.

linux.summary: shred/wipefs/nvme sanitize/cryptsetup luksErase per SP 800-88.

title: Media Marking
statement: Mark media containing CUI with distribution limitations, handling caveats, and applicable CUI markings.

title: Media Transport
statement: Protect, control, account for, and document CUI media during transport outside controlled areas.

linux.summary: Partial: encrypt removable media (LUKS) before transport.

title: Media Use
statement: Restrict or prohibit ODP types of system media; prohibit removable media without an identifiable owner.

odps.defaultValue: unmanaged USB mass storage; U3; writable optical on servers

linux.summary: usbguard + blacklist usb_storage unless an owner-tagged device is allowed.

remediate.title: optional usb_storage blacklist
remediate.notes: Skip on admin jump hosts that need USB.

title: System Backup – Cryptographic Protection
statement: Protect confidentiality of backup information; cryptographic mechanisms at backup storage locations.

linux.summary: restic/borg to an encrypted repo, or tar | gpg, or LUKS on backup target.

title: Personnel Screening
statement: Screen individuals prior to authorizing access; rescreen per ODP conditions.

title: Personnel Termination and Transfer
statement: On termination: disable access within ODP time, revoke authenticators, retrieve security property.
On transfer: review need and modify authorizations.

linux.summary: On termination: usermod -L, chage -E 0, ssh key revoke, kill sessions.

title: Physical Access Authorizations
statement: Develop/approve/maintain facility access list; issue credentials; review at ODP frequency; remove when no longer required.

title: Monitoring Physical Access
statement: Monitor physical access to detect/respond to incidents; review logs at ODP frequency and on ODP events.

title: Alternate Work Site
statement: Determine allowed alternate work sites; employ ODP security requirements there.

odps.defaultValue: full-disk encryption, VPN, no local CUI copies, privacy screen

title: Physical Access Control
statement: Enforce authorizations at entry/exit; maintain logs; escort visitors; secure keys; control physical access to output devices.

title: Access Control for Transmission
statement: Control physical access to distribution and transmission lines within organizational facilities.

title: Risk Assessment
statement: Assess risk (including supply-chain) of unauthorized CUI disclosure; update at ODP frequency.

title: Vulnerability Monitoring and Scanning
statement: Monitor/scan at ODP frequency and when new vulns are identified; remediate within ODP times; update scan signatures.

linux.summary: dnf-automatic security; oscap; optional OpenSCAP + lynis. OVAL feeds.

audit.title: dnf-automatic
audit.command: systemctl is-enabled dnf-automatic.timer || systemctl is-enabled dnf-automatic-install.timer

title: Risk Response
statement: Respond to findings from assessments, monitoring, and audits (POA&M only if mitigation is not immediate).

title: Security Assessment
statement: Assess security requirements at ODP frequency to determine whether they are satisfied.

title: Plan of Action and Milestones
statement: Develop POA&Ms for weaknesses; update from assessments, audits, and continuous monitoring.

title: Continuous Monitoring
statement: Develop and implement a system-level continuous-monitoring strategy including ongoing monitoring and assessments.

linux.summary: Partial: auditd + aide.timer + dnf-automatic + osquery/oscap timers.

audit.title: aide timer
audit.command: systemctl is-enabled aide.timer || crontab -l | grep aide

title: Information Exchange
statement: Approve/manage CUI exchange via ODP agreement types; document interfaces, requirements, responsibilities; review at ODP frequency.

linux.summary: Partial: firewalld zones per peer; documented ISA path in /etc/nist/exchanges/.

title: Boundary Protection
statement: Monitor/control communications at external and key internal managed interfaces; separate public subnets; connect externally only through managed boundary devices.

linux.summary: firewalld with public vs trusted zones; no unexpected forwarding; nft counters.

title: Information in Shared System Resources
statement: Prevent unauthorized and unintended information transfer via shared system resources.

linux.summary: kernel.dmesg_restrict, kernel.kptr_restrict, hardened_usercopy; no world-readable /tmp leftovers.

title: Network Communications – Deny by Default – Allow by Exception
statement: Deny network communications traffic by default and allow by exception.

linux.summary: firewalld target DROP; no ACCEPT any any; ssh/https allow-by-exception.

title: Transmission and Storage Confidentiality
statement: Implement cryptographic mechanisms to prevent unauthorized disclosure of CUI during transmission and while in storage.

linux.summary: FIPS crypto-policies; sshd Ciphers/MACs/Kex; TLS 1.2+; LUKS for data at rest.

title: Network Disconnect
statement: Terminate the network connection associated with a communications session at end of session or after ODP inactivity.

linux.summary: sshd ClientAlive + TCPKeepAlive no; nft ct timeout.

title: Cryptographic Key Establishment and Management
statement: Establish and manage keys per ODP generation/distribution/storage/access/destruction requirements.

odps.defaultValue: FIPS 140-3; ssh-keygen; LUKS; no keys in world-readable files; destroy via shred/luksErase

linux.summary: ssh-keygen ed25519/ecdsa; umask on keys; no world-readable host keys; optional tang/clevis.

title: Cryptographic Protection
statement: Implement ODP types of cryptography to protect CUI confidentiality. FIPS-validated is recommended.

linux.summary: FIPS 140-3 via crypto-policies FIPS and fips-mode-setup; OpenSSL FIPS provider.

title: Collaborative Computing Devices and Applications
statement: Prohibit remote activation of collaborative devices except ODP exceptions; provide explicit indication of use to physically present users.

odps.defaultValue: none on CUI servers; user-initiated conferencing on workstations

linux.summary: Blacklist uvcvideo/snd-usb-audio on servers; webcam LED policy on workstations.

title: Mobile Code
statement: Define acceptable mobile code; authorize, monitor, and control its use.

linux.summary: Partial: no java applets; browser policy; signed modules only (module.sig_enforce).

title: Session Authenticity
statement: Protect the authenticity of communications sessions.

linux.summary: sshd rekey, TLS session tickets off or rotated; nginx ssl_protocols TLSv1.2 TLSv1.3.

title: Flaw Remediation
statement: Identify, report, and correct system flaws; install security-relevant updates within ODP time of release.

linux.summary: dnf-automatic security installs; yum-cron equivalent.

title: Malicious Code Protection
statement: Implement malware protection at entry/exit; update as releases are available; scan on ODP frequency and in real time; block/quarantine on detection.

linux.summary: clamav + freshclam; optional rkhunter. Prefer FIPS-capable AV on CUI hosts.

audit.title: clamd
audit.command: systemctl is-active clamd@scan || systemctl is-active clamav-daemon

title: Security Alerts, Advisories, and Directives
statement: Receive external alerts/advisories/directives on an ongoing basis; generate and disseminate internal ones as necessary.

linux.summary: Partial: dnf-automatic + mail from auditd; subscribe to CISA feeds organizationally.

title: System Monitoring
statement: Monitor to detect attacks/indicators and unauthorized connections; identify unauthorized use; monitor inbound/outbound traffic for unusual activity.

linux.summary: auditd + AIDE + firewalld logging + optional osquery. FIM lives here in r3 (r2 3.14.7 withdrawn).

title: Withdrawn
withdrawnReason: Incorporated into 03.14.06 (this is where FIM/AIDE belongs in r3).

title: Information Management and Retention
statement: Manage and retain CUI in the system and CUI output per applicable law, policy, and operational requirements.

linux.summary: Partial: tmpwatch/tmpfiles.d for scratch; CUI retention is a records schedule.

title: Policy and Procedures
statement: Develop, document, and disseminate policies and procedures needed to satisfy CUI security requirements; review at ODP frequency.

title: System Security Plan
statement: Develop an SSP covering components, information types, threats, environment, requirements, safeguards, roles, and other relevant information; review at ODP frequency; protect from unauthorized disclosure.

title: Rules of Behavior
statement: Establish rules of behavior; provide to individuals requiring access; obtain documented acknowledgement before CUI access; review at ODP frequency.

title: Security Engineering Principles
statement: Apply ODP systems security engineering principles to development or modification of the system.

odps.defaultValue: SP 800-160 layered protections, threat modeling, secure SDLC, least functionality

title: Unsupported System Components
statement: Replace components when vendor support ends; provide mitigation or alternate support if they cannot be replaced.

linux.summary: dnf needs-restarting; no EL that is EOL; rpm -q --changelog for unmaintained packages.

title: External System Services
statement: Require external service providers processing CUI to comply with ODP security requirements; document shared roles; monitor compliance.

odps.defaultValue: Flow down 800-171r3; no CUI in non-FIPS SaaS; logging to org SIEM

title: Supply Chain Risk Management Plan
statement: Develop an SCRM plan covering R&D through disposal; review at ODP frequency; protect from unauthorized disclosure.

title: Acquisition Strategies, Tools, and Methods
statement: Develop and implement acquisition strategies, contract tools, and procurement methods to identify, protect against, and mitigate supply-chain risks.

title: Supply Chain Requirements and Processes
statement: Establish a process to identify/address supply-chain weaknesses; enforce ODP security requirements to protect against supply-chain risks.

odps.defaultValue: provenance, signed packages (rpm keys), no untrusted COPR, vetted vendors
